statements.impact_statement: Both images are gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot plus one program: /usr/local/bin/ferroehr in ferroehr, /usr/local/bin/ferroehr-viewer in ferroehr-viewer. That program is the only ELF executable in each image (no shell, no ldd, no setuid or setgid file). On amd64 and arm64 alike its DT_NEEDED list is libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader, with no RPATH or RUNPATH, and it imports no dlopen. Every libc function it calls, its statically linked C code included, is an undefined dynamic symbol; the one name it resolves at run time through dlsym is __pthread_get_minstack (Rust std). The import table is therefore the complete list of glibc entry points it reaches. Neither binary imports glob, glob64 or wordexp (the libc entry points that run the glob matcher). No libc function either binary imports runs the glob matcher, so pattern matching in both programs is Rust code and the libc glob implementation is never called.

The uncontrolled recursion is in check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1 in posix/regexec.c, reached only through the POSIX regex API. glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22850) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability: it describes a way to defeat the stack protector after an attacker already has a stack buffer overflow in the process. The thread-stack layout it relies on is fixed by nptl when a thread starts; no request data an attacker sends reaches it. Using it needs a separate memory-corruption defect in /usr/local/bin/ferroehr or /usr/local/bin/ferroehr-viewer, which would be a finding of its own. Neither binary has a setuid or setgid bit and both run as the non-root user 65532.

On amd64 and arm64 alike its DT_NEEDED list is libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader, with no RPATH or RUNPATH, and it imports no dlopen. Every libc function it calls, its statically linked C code included, is an undefined dynamic symbol; the one name it resolves at run time through dlsym is __pthread_get_minstack (Rust std). The import table is therefore the complete list of glibc entry points it reaches. The attack needs a victim to run ldd, or otherwise have the loader map, an attacker-supplied ELF file. The image has no ldd and no shell, and the loader maps only the program and the three libraries above, all read-only files in the image; neither binary imports dlopen, so it never asks the loader to map a file of an attacker's choosing. Upstream does not treat this as a vulnerability (sourceware bug 22851).

glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22852) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability: it describes how the reuse of cached thread stacks and heaps can make addresses easier to guess, which only matters to an attacker who already holds a memory-corruption primitive. Thread stacks and heap arenas are placed by nptl and malloc; no request data an attacker sends chooses their placement. Exploiting it needs a separate memory-corruption defect in either binary, which would be a finding of its own.

glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22853) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability; the glibc position is that an ASLR bypass is not a vulnerability by itself. Guessing the heap address of a thread made by pthread_create helps only an attacker who already holds a memory-corruption primitive in the process. No request data an attacker sends controls where nptl places a thread's heap, and exploiting it needs a separate memory-corruption defect in either binary, which would be a finding of its own.

The traversal is in guess_category_value (intl/dcigettext.c), which appends the LANGUAGE environment variable to the message catalog path (GLIBC-SA-2026-0025). Neither binary imports a gettext function; both reach glibc's message lookup only through the translated strings of __xpg_strerror_r, perror and gai_strerror. guess_category_value returns the current LC_MESSAGES locale name before it reads LANGUAGE when that name is C or C.<encoding>. A process starts in the C locale (ISO C 7.11.1.1) and leaves it only through setlocale, newlocale or uselocale, which neither binary imports, so the locale stays C, LANGUAGE is never read and no message catalog is opened, whatever the container environment holds.

That program is the only ELF executable in each image (no shell, no ldd, no setuid or setgid file). On amd64 and arm64 alike its DT_NEEDED list is libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader, with no RPATH or RUNPATH, and it imports no dlopen. Every libc function it calls, its statically linked C code included, is an undefined dynamic symbol; the one name it resolves at run time through dlsym is __pthread_get_minstack (Rust std). The import table is therefore the complete list of glibc entry points it reaches. Both binaries import getaddrinfo (and __res_init), and every system name lookup they make (the server resolving its PostgreSQL host, either program resolving its OIDC issuer) initialises the glibc stub resolver from /etc/resolv.conf through NSS 'hosts: files dns'. A search domain of roughly 200 characters or more in that file, or in LOCALDOMAIN, aborts the process on the next lookup (GLIBC-SA-2026-0021). The image ships no /etc/resolv.conf: the container runtime writes it, Kubernetes from the node's file and the pod's dnsConfig, so the search list comes from the deployment's DNS configuration. When that configuration takes search domains from DHCP or a VPN server, an attacker on that network can stop the server or the viewer. The fix is in glibc 2.45; Debian trixie has not shipped it (no-dsa) and the distroless base has no newer digest.
statements.action_statement: Keep the search list in the container's /etc/resolv.conf under the operator's control: on Kubernetes set the pod's dnsPolicy and dnsConfig (or the kubelet --resolv-conf file) from trusted configuration, and on Docker or Podman pass --dns-search, so no search list arrives from DHCP or a VPN server on an untrusted network. Do not set LOCALDOMAIN in the container environment, and keep every search domain shorter than 200 characters. Upgrade to the FerroEHR release that rebuilds on a distroless cc-debian13 base carrying the fixed glibc once Debian ships it.

Debian security tracker, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690: an out-of-bounds access in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation, reached by crafted search data in an application compiled with parallel mode (trixie: no DSA, minor issue). The GCC fix, commit c1f32b67510f, changes only include/parallel/search.h, a header template compiled into a program built with _GLIBCXX_PARALLEL and OpenMP. libstdc++.so.6 does not contain it: its only __gnu_parallel exports are _Settings::get and _Settings::set (nm -D on the rc8 images). Both images are gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot plus one program, /usr/local/bin/ferroehr in ferroehr and /usr/local/bin/ferroehr-viewer in ferroehr-viewer, the only ELF executable in each image. That program is Rust: on amd64 and arm64 alike its DT_NEEDED list is libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader, with no RPATH or RUNPATH; it imports no C++ symbol (no _Z name, no GLIBCXX or CXXABI version) and no dlopen, so it contains no libstdc++ template code and can never map libstdc++.so.6. The program also imports no OpenMP symbol (no GOMP_ or omp_ name), so it is not built in parallel mode. No copy of the defective code exists in either image. gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1 and libgomp1 are reported only because they come from the same gcc-14 source package; libgcc_s.so.1, the one of them the program loads, holds the unwinder.

The ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer images of FerroEHR 5.6.3 and every earlier release are built on a gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot digest that carries zlib1g 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+b1. That version has the infinite loop in crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64. Neither program in those images maps the Debian zlib: libz.so.1 is not in the DT_NEEDED list of /usr/local/bin/ferroehr or /usr/local/bin/ferroehr-viewer on amd64 or arm64, neither imports dlopen, and their compression is Rust code (zlib-rs and miniz_oxide), as version 5 of this document recorded and the release's linkage check verified. Debian publishes the fix in trixie-security as 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 and the distroless base of 2026-11-08 carries it, so the finding is fixed by a rebuild and is not argued away. FerroEHR 5.7.0 and later releases are built on that base and carry no affected version.

That program is the only ELF executable in each image (no shell, no openssl command, no setuid or setgid file). The flaw is in the AES-GCM-SIV cipher of OpenSSL 3.5.7 (libcrypto), which treats a zero-length additional authenticated data input wrongly (OpenSSL security advisory of 2026-11-10). Only a process that loads libcrypto.so.3 and selects AES-GCM-SIV reaches it, and neither program loads it; Debian has no fix for trixie, and the statement goes when the base image carries one.

Debian security tracker, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115819, and GLIBC-SA-2026-0027: the wide scanf family (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf, vwscanf) writes one null byte past a char array filled by a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' modifier (trixie: glibc 2.41-12+deb13u4 unfixed, no DSA, minor issue). The advisory states that the narrow scanf functions are not affected. Both images are gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot plus one program: /usr/local/bin/ferroehr in ferroehr, /usr/local/bin/ferroehr-viewer in ferroehr-viewer, the only ELF executable in each image. On amd64 and arm64 alike its DT_NEEDED list is libgcc_s.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6 and the dynamic loader, with no RPATH or RUNPATH, and it imports no dlopen; the one name it resolves at run time through dlsym is __pthread_get_minstack (Rust std). Every libc function it calls, its statically linked C code included, is an undefined dynamic symbol, so the import table is the complete list of glibc entry points it reaches. That table holds no function of the wide scanf family under any name (plain, __isoc99_ or __isoc23_); its one scanf import is the narrow __isoc23_sscanf (objdump -T on the ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer binaries of the :main images of 2026-11-13, both architectures). No process in either image reaches the defective code.
